findings.text: Core dump output exposes helpers to declare holes and to transfer user memory. A reposition helper derives pending hole length from a target position and current position, a skip helper accumulates relative hole length, and a range helper walks a virtual interval page by page emitting present pages and treating absent pages as holes. The range helper reports binary success and manages its own scratch page.

Format management provides registration that forwards a descriptor to the core registrar as a non prioritized entry, and removal that detaches a descriptor from the shared list under write exclusion. Both manipulate the global format collection.

Standard ELF loader defines paired lifecycle entries. Initialization publishes the ELF format descriptor and signals success. Termination withdraws the same descriptor. The pair governs loader availability.

Position independent ELF handling defines its own lifecycle pair that publishes and withdraws a dedicated format descriptor, with binary loading designated as the recognition entry and core dumping plus a page sized minimum granularity enabled when core support is present.

The dedicated format descriptor holds module ownership and operation pointers for binary loading and, under core support, for core dumping, together with a minimum dump granularity. Unpopulated operations remain absent.
Character addresses use a plain mutable character pointer alias. Load and core diagnostic helpers expand to empty statements that evaluate to nothing, imposing no storage or effects.

Dump segment totals combine recorded virtual area count with architecture extra headers plus an additional notes entry. The header count saturates at the extended numbering threshold, with the full total preserved via a section header extension when saturated. File layout places the ELF header first, followed by program headers, then notes including architecture extras, then page aligned file data and extras, with the extension record at the end when present.

Each virtual area appears as a loadable segment whose file extent covers only dumpable bytes and whose memory extent spans the whole area, whose physical address is cleared, whose alignment matches execution page size, and whose permissions reflect area readability, writability and executability. File offsets progress by dumped extents.

Binary acceptance requires ELF magic over the defined length, executable or shared object type, architecture approval, and mappability of the file. Memory managed builds decline images lacking the position independent marker. Other builds accept only shared object type among those. Displacement classification treats images without the marker or with explicit constant displacement as constant.

Header table loading validates entry size against native program header size and rejects excessive counts bounded by a fixed total size limit. The table is allocated and fully read, with allocation, IO and short read problems all reported as failures. Stack policy and size derive from the first stack indicative entry when present.

Page output flushes pending holes before writing, enforces a total written limit and interruption checks, then advances file position and accounting by a full page on success. Pending holes clear only after successful flushing. Range traversal steps by pages, emitting present pages and skipping absent ones as sparse regions, yielding cooperatively when rescheduling is indicated.

Scratch handling differs by build. A copying variant provides allocation, release, and tolerant copying from source to scratch that signals failure on uncorrectable errors. A pass through variant signals allocation failure, ignores release, and returns the source without copying.
Architecture extension points default to neutral behavior with no extra headers, no extra size, and successful no-op writers for extra headers, data and notes.

User stack preparation aligns the pointer, copies optional platform capability strings, and places executable and optional interpreter load maps with suitable alignment and records their user addresses in the address space context. Space for auxiliary vectors, environment, arguments and count is reserved with wide final alignment, and the saved auxiliary area receives hardware, paging, timing, header location, entry, identity, security and execution metadata.
Format removal excludes concurrent list mutation and traversal by holding the global format write lock across detachment.

Range dumping holds the address space read lock only around page table inspection, acquiring it lazily in killable mode and releasing it before file IO, before cooperative rescheduling, and on all exits. The lock is never retained across blocking output.

Loading advances from validation through interpreter resolution and stack policy choice to irreversible replacement of the address space, followed by mapping, stack establishment, table construction and thread launch. Failures before replacement release tables and interpreter references, but failures after replacement still report errors though the prior image is already gone.

Dumping signals overall note setup outcome rather than full IO success. The marker becomes set once note preparation completes and persists through later output stages, with note state and temporary headers always released before exit.

Output hazards include scratch allocation failure, hole flush failure, written limit overrun, external interruption, tolerant copy failure, and short writes. Absent pages are benign and yield holes, but killed lock acquisition aborts the transfer.

Load hazards include header size mismatch, excessive header count, allocation and IO failures, oversized or unterminated interpreter paths, interpreter access and validation failures, replacement and mapping errors, and table construction errors. Only the earliest interpreter directive takes effect.

The program count saturation threshold is defined by PN_XNUM with value 0xffff, data alignment and minimum dump granularity follow ELF_EXEC_PAGESIZE, dumped areas use type PT_LOAD, and permissions use PF_R plus PF_W plus PF_X corresponding to readable plus writable plus executable areas. Physical address for dumped segments is defined as cleared.

Recognition relies on magic ELFMAG with length SELFMAG, types ET_EXEC and ET_DYN, stack indicative segment PT_GNU_STACK, and stack control values EXSTACK_ENABLE_X plus EXSTACK_DISABLE_X plus EXSTACK_DEFAULT. Unspecified stack size falls back to 131072, path limits follow PATH_MAX and BINPRM_BUF_SIZE, and interpreter names require at least two bytes with termination. Header table total size observes a 65536 byte ceiling, and minimal anonymous stack spans twice page size.

Auxiliary metadata count base is defined by DLINFO_ITEMS with value 15, load maps use structures elf_fdpic_loadmap and elf_fdpic_loadseg, stack frames enforce eight byte intermediate and sixteen byte final alignment, and auxiliary entries convey hardware, paging, timing, header, entry, identity, security and execution facts.

Position independent state uses flags ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_PRESENT plus ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_EXECUTABLE plus ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_CONSTDISP plus ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_EXEC_STACK plus ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_NOEXEC_STACK to mark presence plus executability plus displacement plus stack policy.
